title: Mastering Trabeculectomy: The Gold Standard in Glaucoma Filtration Surgery
summary: Trabeculectomy remains the gold-standard 'filtering surgery' for medically uncontrolled glaucoma, creating a full-thickness fistula to bypass the trabecular meshwork. This guide details the surgical precision required to maintain long-term intraocular pressure (IOP) control.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Trabeculectomy is a guarded filtration procedure. It involves the creation of a partial-thickness scleral flap, an excision of a block of trabecular meshwork and peripheral iris (peripheral iridectomy), and re-suturing the flap to allow aqueous humor to flow from the anterior chamber into a sub-conjunctival space (bleb).

sections.title: Surgical Technique Workflow
content: 1. Conjunctival peritomy: Limbal-based or Fornix-based incision.
2. Hemostasis: Cautery application to sclera to ensure a dry field.
3. Mitomycin-C (MMC) application: 0.2-0.4 mg/ml for 1-3 minutes under conjunctiva.
4. Scleral flap creation: 4x4mm partial thickness trapezoid or triangular flap.
5. Sclerostomy: Excision of the block containing trabecular meshwork.
6. Peripheral Iridectomy (PI): Prevention of iris plugging the sclerostomy.
7. Scleral flap closure: Titratable 10-0 nylon sutures to regulate aqueous flow.
8. Water-tight conjunctival closure.

content.explanation: Fibrosis (subconjunctival), Infection (late blebitis), Leaks (seidel positive), Tenon's cyst (encapsulation), Epiretinal membrane/maculopathy (hypotony), Retinal detachment.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Follow-up
content: Slit-lamp examination: Assess Seidel's test (Fluorescein dilution), bleb morphology (Height, Vascularity, Area).
Gonioscopy: Verify patency of the internal sclerostomy.
Anterior Segment OCT (AS-OCT): Visualize internal filtration pathway and fluid flow.
Visual Field testing: Monitor progression post-IOP stabilization.
IOP Monitoring: Diurnal curves in the first week post-op.

sections.title: Red Flag Warnings
content: Seidel positive test: Immediate patch or suturing required to prevent endophthalmitis.
Flat Anterior Chamber (AC): Risk of corneal endothelial decompensation and peripheral anterior synechiae.
Late-onset purulent discharge: Rule out bleb-associated endophthalmitis immediately (Ocular emergency).
Extreme hypotony (IOP < 5 mmHg): Risk of suprachoroidal hemorrhage.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: MMC usage significantly improves surgical success but increases the risk of thin, avascular 'cystic' blebs.
For fornix-based flaps, ensure the Tenon's capsule is well-anchored to the limbus to prevent retraction.
Adjustable sutures are preferred for post-operative titration of aqueous outflow.
Laser Suture Lysis (LSL): Use argon laser (typically 500-1000mW) 1-2 weeks post-op to increase flow if IOP is elevated.
The 'Needling' procedure: Effective intervention for encapsulated (Tenon's) cysts appearing 4-8 weeks post-op.
